lines.text: The youngest Measurer didn't measure anybody that afternoon. She played tag with the village children instead. And Ash followed her everywhere, exactly as I'd warned.
By the end of the day, she had lost every game, and fourteen children were sitting on my dog.
You're not very good at being frightening.
I'm not very good at being a Measurer. Please don't tell Magister Hask.
Your village is strange, my lord. Everyone is so healthy. In my village, the children coughed all winter. Here they run like deer.
Why did you join the Order?
I have a little sister. Nell. She was five when the Measurers came to our village. They said she was special. Hollow-born. They said the Order would take care of her.
They promised I could visit her, once I earned my silver lens.
I earned it last spring. I have asked to see her eleven times. They always say, next year.
Hollow-born. The same word Ilse had used for me. I didn't say anything. I couldn't.
She carved me this bird. She said it would fly to me if she ever needed help. Silly, isn't it.
Ash put his enormous head in her lap, the way he always did when someone in the keep was sad.
That night, I couldn't stop thinking about it. Somewhere, the Order was keeping a little girl called Nell. And if Ilse was right, it wanted to keep me too.
Out in the Measurers' camp, one lamp burned very late.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter twenty-one, coming soon.
